blockNote: Mystic-statue reward ceremony (scene $FD, Bank 00, 52569-53033). Six copies of this actor spawn in scene $FD, one per pedestal; only the copy whose table index equals globalScriptIndex ($0AAC) runs the ceremony, the others stay hidden or show a statue that was collected before. Scene $FD lists nothing but these six actors (no player, no camera).
=== TRIGGER ===

Six scripts queue scene $FD with COP QueueMapChange: index 0 gs2E_crew2 (Gold Ship), 1 sg55_mystic_statue (Viper), 2 mu66_rama_spirits (Mu), 3 gw8A_sand_fanger (Great Wall), 4 pyDD_mystic_statue (Mummy Queen), 5 btDE_olman (Babel). Each first writes globalScriptIndex = its index, sourceSceneId ($0B12) = its own scene ($2E, $55, $66, $8A, $CD, $DE) and the return position in $0B08-$0B10 (tile X, tile Y, scroll parameters).
=== TABLE statue_reward_00CE97 ===
6 entries of 4 bytes (3 fields + 1 tail byte, never read by the two actors):
| Index | Flag | Sprite | Match | Boss / event | Trigger script |
| 0 | $F8 | $3A | $00 | Gold Ship event | gs2E_crew2.asm |
| 1 | $F9 | $3B | $01 | Viper | sg55_mystic_statue.asm |
| 2 | $FA | $3C | $02 | Mu (Rama's spirits) | mu66_rama_spirits.asm |
| 3 | $FB | $3D | $03 | Sand Fanger | gw8A_sand_fanger.asm |
| 4 | $FC | $3E | $04 | Mummy Queen | pyDD_mystic_statue.asm |
| 5 | $FD | $3F | $05 | Olman (Babel) | btDE_olman.asm |

Flag = event flag index: flag N is bit (N AND 7) of byte $0A00 + N / 8, so $F8-$FD are bits 0-5 of the single byte $0A1F. Sprite = animation index ($28) in inventory_spritemap. Match = the globalScriptIndex value for which this entry is the statue being awarded (it equals the row number).
=== ACTOR FLOW ===

1. Entry: joypadMaskStd |= $FFFC (every button hidden; this build's value, the vanilla $FFF0 is rewritten by transforms.json, probably to cover the remapped X bit $0004), NudgePosition(8, 8) plus (0, -8) when bit 4 of the spawn parameter is set (same record encoding and positions as inventory_statue_slot), metasprite inventory_spritemap. Initial flags $3000: hidden, and running in the display-filtered pass.

2. Screen setup by direct register writes: BG1 tilemap at VRAM word $0800 (BG1SC $08), BG2 tilemap at $0C00 (BG2SC $0C), main screen BG1 + BG2 + OBJ (TM $13), sub screen BG1 + OBJ (TS $11), colour math with the sub screen as the source (CGWSEL $82) added onto BG2 only (CGADSUB $02). There is no BGMODE write. srcCacheBgD+1 ($0676-$0677) is cleared to invalidate graphics cache slot D.

3. Every copy: index = low nibble of the parameter. TestFlagRaw(flag): set -> StatueRewardAlreadyClaimed (statue shown, idle). Otherwise match against globalScriptIndex: different -> StatueRewardWrongTab (stays hidden, idle).

4. The matching copy: SetFlagRaw (statue collected for good; inventory_statue_slot shows it from now on), animation frame set (still hidden), then 8 StatueRewardOrbitalSparkle actors with start angles $21, $41, ... $E1, $0101 (the loop ends when the angle word reaches $0101; only the low byte is an angle, so they are $20 apart).

5. Waiting: globalScriptIndex becomes a 180-frame countdown. Each frame it is decremented; at zero the ceremony jumps straight to step 7 (no confetti). While IsMusicPlaying (SPC transfer pending or the display-filter bit set) it waits. When that ends the counter is zeroed, WaitByte $0F, sound $2525 on both channels, then the orbitDiameter of the LAST sparkle spawned is polled each frame until it is 0.

6. Reveal: the hidden bit is cleared and 60 StatueRewardConfettiBurst actors are spawned, one per frame (LoopEnd yields every iteration). Each burst tests frameCounter AND 3 on its first tick and dies at once unless that is 0, so only about one burst in four is visible.

7. Exit: sceneNext = sourceSceneId (a nonzero sceneNext starts the scene change), warpDestX / warpDestY = $0B08 / $0B0C x 16, warpFacing = 3, warpScrollParams = $0B10, gfxCacheIdxA = $0002 (exit effect 2 = mosaic, enter effect 0 = fade) and gfxCacheIdxB = $0303 (speed 3 for both).

StatueRewardAlreadyClaimed: This statue was collected before the ceremony started: reached by JMP with X = table byte offset and the actor slot on the stack. Sets the frame, shows the statue and idles.
StatueRewardWrongTab: A statue that is not the one being awarded (match byte differs from globalScriptIndex, and its own flag is still clear): restores X and idles hidden. The name says 'tab' but there is no tab in scene $FD.
statue_reward_00CE97: Statue table: flag index, sprite (animation index), match value and one tail byte per entry. Read by this actor and inventory_statue_slot (index x 4).
StatueRewardOrbitalSparkle: Sparkle that spirals in toward the statue. Start diameter $FC, start angle = the value the ceremony wrote into its $26. Each tick: position = the ceremony actor + orbit(angle, diameter) (ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef), angle + 4, diameter - 2; the actor dies once the diameter is 0 (about 126 ticks).
StatueRewardConfettiBurst: One short effect at the statue: X within -8..+7 px, Y 8 px up, frame #02 played once. It runs only when frameCounter AND 3 = 0 on its first tick; otherwise it dies immediately.

blockNote: Development tool: walks the ROM for COP PrintDialogString calls and shows each dialog string (Bank 0B, 778693-778807). No scene, script or table references it (an unscened actor).

HOW IT FINDS STRINGS: the word $BF02 is the byte pair 02 BF, a COP instruction with signature $BF = PrintDialogString (copdef), followed by its 2-byte operand, a pointer to the string in the script's own bank (&DialogString). The scanner compares a word at every offset, reads the operand after a hit and shows the string through DialogStringRenderer with DBR = the scanned bank, so the pointer resolves in the right bank. The old header called $BF02 a 'dialog string header marker'.

POINTER TEST: IsStringPointer sets carry for values BELOW 0x8000 and clears it for 0x8000 and up, and the caller skips a hit on carry set (BCS). A string is therefore shown only when the operand is at least 0x8000 (a LoROM address). The old header and the inline notes had this reversed.

SCAN RANGE: the bank counter $24 is a 16-bit word that starts at $85 and is incremented per bank. The loop ends only when it equals $000C, which happens after the word wraps through $FFFF. Each pass takes the LOW byte as the bank (PHA / PLB), so banks $85-$FF come first, then banks $00-$FF again and again; the old 'banks $85 to $0B' (and the doc's '$85-$8C') do not match the code. Banks after the first are scanned from offset $0000, which on LoROM is not ROM for banks $80-$BF. In practice the halt loop is not reached.

SAVED STATE: $0100 = the scan offset after a hit, $0102 = a 16-bit copy of the stack top (the bank byte plus the low byte of the pointer). Only system_core's startup check reads $0100 (a leftover resume test).
START: runs only while worldReadyFlag ($0654) is nonzero and positive (negative = loading); until then it returns every frame.

IsStringPointer: Carry SET for a value below 0x8000, carry CLEAR for 0x8000 and up. The caller treats carry set as 'not a LoROM address, skip it', so only operands of 0x8000 or more are shown.

blockNote: Shadow's palette shimmer (Bank 02, 176654-176798): a hidden companion that animates the player's OBJ palette 0 (colours $81-$8F) while the player is Shadow (characterForm 2).

SPAWN: PlayerCharacterDef (SpawnListAppend, so it is appended at the end of the actor list) and the two Dark Space transformations in sE6_gaia (Transform_WillToShadow, Transform_FreedanToShadow), which spawn it just before they set characterForm = 2; the new actor runs later in the same tick, after the form is set. All three use flags $2800: hidden ($2000) plus $0800, so it also runs in the cutscene-only passes. Init dies at once when characterForm is not 2.

STRUCTURE: Init spawns ShadowShimmerCycleA with SpawnAfterMarked (a marked child dies with its parent). This actor never touches the palette: it only points the child at one of three routines by writing the child's entry word ($0000,Y) and clearing its waitCounter ($0008,Y). The child is found through $06 (the actor-list successor), which is the child because SpawnAfter inserts it directly behind its spawner.
- ShadowShimmerCycleA: bundle #23 in a loop (eight strips, wait 2 each)
- ShadowShimmerCycleB: bundle #24 in a loop (eight strips, waits 0 and 1 alternating: a faster cycle)
- ShadowShimmerNop: yields every frame, no palette change
Both bundles write colours $81-$8F (15 colours, size byte $1D); bundle #23 is also the Shadow palette that global_ambient_dispatcher loads at spawn.

STATES: Idle (cycle A) and Active (cycle B). Idle -> Active when playerSpeedEw or playerSpeedNs is nonzero, or when flag byte #00 is set. Active -> Idle when both speeds are zero and flag #00 is clear. The speed words are not set by ordinary walking (walking uses the joypad velocity of player_move_controller); they are nonzero during slope and ramp slides and in run / slide moves, so cycle B plays then. Flag #00 is a general per-scene flag (scene_lifecycle clears it at scene setup; scene_flag_init sets it in 26 scene lists; some scripts set and clear it) that player_character also reads to pick Shadow's idle, ladder and shimmy-detach sprites; where it is set, this actor stays in Active. What the flag means is open (OQ-I030-1; here OQ-I048-1).

GUARD (ShadowShimmerGuard, called every frame from both states): characterForm no longer 2 -> pop the return address and Die (the marked child dies too). Player Flags10 bit $0040 (dead: set when HP reaches 0 by combat_collision and by GameOverSequence; combat_collision also calls it the orb state) -> point the child at ShadowShimmerNop and run SetEntryHere + RTL. The saved entry is that RTL, so the states are never run again for the rest of the scene visit and the palette stays on whatever strip was showing.

ShadowShimmerInit: Spawned by PlayerCharacterDef and by the two Dark Space transformations to Shadow. Dies at once unless characterForm is 2, otherwise spawns the palette child (cycle A) and falls into ShadowShimmerIdle.
ShadowShimmerIdle: Idle state: point the child at cycle A and restart it, then each frame: guard, then switch to Active when a speed word is nonzero or flag byte #00 is set. Plain walking leaves both speed words at zero.
ShadowShimmerActive: Active state: point the child at cycle B and restart it, then each frame: guard, stay while a speed word is nonzero, go back to Idle when both are zero and flag byte #00 is clear.
ShadowShimmerGuard: Called with JSR from both states every frame. Form no longer Shadow: pop the return address and Die. Player Flags10 bit $0040 (dead) set: pop the return address, point the child at ShadowShimmerNop and execute SetEntryHere + RTL (the saved entry is the RTL, so this actor never runs its states again). Otherwise RTS.
ShadowShimmerCycleA: Child routine: play palette bundle #23 (eight strips on colours $81-$8F, wait 2 each) in an endless loop.
ShadowShimmerCycleB: Child routine: play palette bundle #24 (eight strips on colours $81-$8F, waits 0 and 1 alternating) in an endless loop.
ShadowShimmerNop: Child routine: yield every frame, no palette change. The colours stay as the last strip left them.
